svg.title: Bits, operators and masks
svg.desc: Four panels for the Lab 02 theory. 1: the byte 0x2F as eight bits with weights 128…1, two hex digits of four bits each, decimal 47. 2: −5 in two's complement: 5, flip the bits, add 1, giving 0xFB; the same byte is 251 as uint8_t and −5 as int8_t because bit 7 weighs −128. 3: a = 0xCA and b = 0xA6 bit by bit through &, |, ^, ~; the shifts a << 1 and a >> 1, where the bit that drops out goes into flag C; the precedence trap x & 1 == 0. 4: the byte 0b1011'10'01 split into opcode, dest and src fields by a shift and a mask; set, clear and test a flag bit; the high nibble of an ember opcode is its group.
svg.text: A byte is eight bits. A bitwise operator works on each bit separately.
decimal: 32 + 8 + 4 + 2 + 1, the weights of the ones
The same byte 0xFB, two readings. Only the weight of bit 7 differs:
3. Six operators, each bit on its own
Each column ignores its neighbours. Bit 6: a = 1, b = 0 → & gives 0, | and ^ give 1.

text.tspan: SHL A: bit 7 drops into C
SHR A: bit 0 drops into C

svg.text: For unsigned: x << n = x · 2ⁿ, x >> n = x / 2ⁿ
Precedence: x & 1 == 0 parses as x & (1 == 0) = x & 0 = 0, always false. Write (x & 1) == 0.
Width: 1 << 31 on an int lands in the sign bit, 1 << 32 is UB. For bits, use unsigned: 1u << n.
4. Shift and mask: split a byte into fields
1. shift the field down to bit 0
A flag bit: set, clear, test
In ember: the high nibble of an opcode is its group
0x10 ADD · 0x11 SUB · … · 0x16 SHL A · 0x17 SHR A
The whole byte says which instruction it is; see the ISA table.
